title: Rapid, in-situ fungal DNA extraction (Toothpick Method)
author: Harte Singer

steps.title: Prepare and label PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Label or mark 0.2 uL individual attached-cap PCR tubes to ensure samples can be easily referenced.

steps.title: Add XNA buffer to tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 30 µL of XNA buffer into each PCR tube and close the caps.

substeps.instruction: Pour an appropriate volume of XNA buffer into a brand-new reagent reservoir, adding a little extra to account for pipetting error.
Use a 5-50 uL 8-channel micropipette (or a p200 single-channel micropipette) to add 30 µL of buffer per tube.

steps.title: Sample fungal tissue
steps.instruction: Collect a small amount of fungal tissue using a fresh toothpick.

substeps.instruction: Remove the wrapper of a fresh toothpick by pushing the toothpick through the wrapper, avoiding touching the exposed toothpick.
Dip or scratch the fertile surface of the mushroom with the toothpick to get some tissue stuck to the rough surface.
Ensure only a small amount of 'schmutz' is collected; avoid getting a chunk of tissue to prevent PCR inhibition.

steps.title: Extract DNA in-situ
steps.instruction: Transfer the sampled tissue into the buffer and mix.

substeps.instruction: Open the cap of a PCR tube containing buffer.
Insert the toothpick tip and swirl in the buffer for 3 seconds.
Remove and discard the toothpick, close the cap, and record the sample location in notes.

steps.title: Incubate and lyse samples
steps.instruction: Process the tubes using a microcentrifuge and thermal cycler.

substeps.instruction: Spin down all filled tubes in a microcentrifuge for 10 seconds.
Place tubes in a PCR thermal cycler and incubate at 95 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Store samples (Optional)
steps.instruction: Store samples if not proceeding immediately to the next step.

substeps.instruction: Store samples at -20 °C (though they are shelf-stable at room temperature for at least 8 weeks if covered with buffer).

steps.title: Dilute samples (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform an optional dilution of the extracted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Pour Low TE (recommended) or molecular-grade water into a brand new reagent reservoir.
Using a 50-300 uL 8-channel micropipette (or p200 single-channel), add 80 µL of the liquid to each tube.
Expel the liquid smoothly without splashing or dribbling.

steps.title: Final spin down
steps.instruction: Spin tubes down in a microcentrifuge for 10 seconds to bring all liquid and sample to the bottom of the tube.
